A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChartAgent research. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, trajectory analyses, and results on a curated 125-example internal dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds tolerance sensitivity results, manual validation studies, and qualitative agent trajectories.

M1.justification: The ReAct reasoning loop, metadata routing, fallback, tool definitions, and prompts are retained. Appendix F.3 clarifies existing self-verification behavior. The parallel execution timing configuration does not establish a revised reasoning algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same ChartBench coverage, 1,152 ChartX pairs, and 125-example internal benchmark. v2 adds curation details and analyses within retained coverage; it does not introduce another evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix L.9 adds o3 to the runtime comparison, whereas v1 Appendix J.9 compares timing only with GPT-4o. The accuracy comparator sets are retained, including the internal benchmark's GPT-5 comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation at six numerical tolerances, normalization checks on 100 examples per dataset, and complexity-label validation by two annotators reviewing 10 examples per category and dimension. It also reports parallel and nonparallel timing conditions. The principal dataset selections and 5% accuracy protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices H–K add substantive checks of normalization correctness, tolerance sensitivity, and automatic complexity labels, plus detailed cases illustrating successful reasoning, recovery, and fallback. These extend the analyses beyond v1's retained ablations, tool-use statistics, and failure taxonomy.

E5.justification: Appendix J newly quantifies human–automatic disagreement in complexity labels using two annotators, adding an annotation-reliability assessment absent from v1. Seed 42 remains unchanged; neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds tolerance-dependent accuracy, over 97% normalization correctness, 8% complexity-label disagreement, and numerous example predictions. Timing estimates change from approximately 125 seconds for ChartAgent and 12 seconds for GPT-4o to 90 seconds nonparallel, 30 seconds parallel, and 6–10 seconds respectively. These are revised reports without sufficiently matched settings to establish a controlled speedup. Existing benchmark accuracy tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The state-update formulation and mathematical operations are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the tolerance sweep varies an existing evaluation rule rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same visually grounded agent framework, headline accuracy gains, broad chart-type coverage, and plug-and-play generalization claims. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of component reuse and agent-driven verification, and discusses missing intermediate ground truth, manually designed tools, and latency-reduction strategies. It removes inconsistent limitations about evaluating only GPT-4o and lacking a held-out dataset, while newly asserting definite exclusion of benchmarks from GPT-4o training based on cutoff dates.

D1.justification: v2 documents exact versions for additional already-evaluated baselines, selection details for the existing internal dataset, and the shared 15-step ablation limit. It removes the specific promise to release resources upon acceptance, although a general research-release statement remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to VideoAgent, VideoAgent2, and additional model cards, including GPT-5 and o1. These provide limited support for evaluation positioning and model documentation; the central relationship to chart VQA and tool-augmented agents remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds numbered subsections and targeted rewrites of related work, tool explanations, and limitations. New appendix sections improve navigation, but much of the main narrative and the extensive prompt appendix remain textually unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 introduces the tolerance table and Figures 11–26, with extensive trajectory diagrams, intermediate visual outputs, recovery illustrations, and prediction panels. Existing chart-type figures are reordered, while retained tool-use and failure figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through manual validation, detailed trajectories, and expanded limitations. However, its new Table 6 reports Pixtral at 44.11% under 5% tolerance versus 40.50% in retained Table 1, and DePlot accuracy decreases from 41.39% at 5% tolerance to 40.33% at 10%. Figure 26 also marks some predictions within the stated tolerance as incorrect. These unresolved problems in the added evidence offset identifiable benefits sufficiently that a reliable net quality judgment is unclear.
